/-!
# Erdős Problem 99

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99)
* [BeFo99] Bezdek, Andr\'{a}s and Fodor, Ferenc, Minimal diameter of certain sets in the plane. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1999), 105-111.
* [Er94b] Erd\H{o}s, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set Metric EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos99

/-- A set has minimum distance $1$ if all pairwise distances are at least $1$,
and the minimum is achieved. -/
def HasMinDist1 (A : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  (∀ᵉ (p ∈ A) (q ∈ A), p ≠ q → dist p q ≥ 1) ∧
  (∃ᵉ (p ∈ A) (q ∈ A), dist p q = 1)

/-- Three points form an equilateral triangle of side length 1. -/
def FormsEquilateralTriangle (p q r : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  dist p q = 1 ∧ dist q r = 1 ∧ dist p r = 1

/-- For sufficiently large n, is it the case that any set of n points with minimum distance $1$
that minimizes diameter must contain an equilateral triangle of side length 1? -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_99 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n → HasMinDist1 A →
      (IsMinOn (fun B: Finset ℝ² => diam (B : Set ℝ²)) {B : Finset ℝ² | B.card = n ∧ HasMinDist1 B} A) →
      ∃ᵉ (p ∈ A) (q ∈ A) (r ∈ A), FormsEquilateralTriangle p q r := by
  sorry

end Erdos99

reformulations.difference: The Lean minimizes over configurations whose minimum separation is exactly 1, rather than merely requiring separation at least 1 as in the packing formulation described in BeFo99. The problem-99 webpage itself already uses the exact-1 normalization.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any finite configuration of at least two points with separation at least 1, its minimum pairwise distance δ exists and satisfies δ ≥ 1. Scaling by 1/δ preserves cardinality, makes the minimum distance exactly 1, and changes diameter D to D/δ ≤ D. Thus an exact-1 minimizer also minimizes among all configurations with separation at least 1. Conversely, a minimizer in the latter family cannot have δ > 1, since scaling would strictly decrease its positive diameter. The minimizer classes therefore coincide for n ≥ 2, which suffices for the eventual statement.

review.notes: All three declarations are faithful to the problem statement; the research-open tag agrees with the current source. Scratch tests in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled with zero errors. They check the Euclidean metric, exclusion of empty and singleton configurations, implicit distinctness of unit-distance vertices, boundedness of every diameter argument, global minimization, the sufficiently-large cutoff, and realizable unit pairs and triangles. Unit pairs were also proved to be genuine minimizers for n=2. The source's n=4 square counterexample does not contradict the eventual quantifier. BeFo99's full text was unavailable, but its abstract was read and no declaration remained unsettled: the main conjecture is explicitly stated in both the problem page and Er94b §3.2. The reviewed file was not modified.
